QuestionStmt.S: For the reaction, $\mathrm{NO_2(g) + CO(g) \rightarrow NO(g) + CO_2(g)}$, rate of formation of $\mathrm{NO(g)}$ is $Y \, \text{mol} \, \text{dm}^{-3} \, \text{s}^{-1}$. Find the rate of disappearance of $\mathrm{CO(g)}$.

Solution.S:
Given reaction:
$$\mathrm{NO_2(g) + CO(g) \rightarrow NO(g) + CO_2(g)}$$

According to NCERT, the rate of a reaction in terms of reactants and products is given by:
$$-\frac{d[\mathrm{NO_2}]}{dt} = -\frac{d[\mathrm{CO}]}{dt} = \frac{d[\mathrm{NO}]}{dt} = \frac{d[\mathrm{CO_2}]}{dt}$$

If the rate of formation of NO is $Y \, \text{mol} \, \text{dm}^{-3} \, \text{s}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{d[\mathrm{NO}]}{dt} = Y$$

So,
$$-\frac{d[\mathrm{CO}]}{dt} = Y$$

This implies,
Rate of disappearance of $\mathrm{CO} = Y \, \text{mol} \, \text{dm}^{-3} \, \text{s}^{-1}$

Correct option: A
